---
title: "Readings — Pooled screens and synthetic libraries"
---

Two decks, one reading list. Read the screening papers for the library: how the pool was made,
how many cells carried each member, and how the counts were turned into a sequencing library.
The biology comes second.

## Building and delivering a pool

**Shalem O, et al. (2014).** *Genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screening in human cells.*
Science 343:84–87.
[doi:10.1126/science.1247005](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1247005) — **start here**

> The lentiCRISPR pooled screen in human cells. Look at how the library was synthesised, how
> coverage was kept, and how the readout was done.

**Sanjana NE, Shalem O, Zhang F (2014).** *Improved vectors and genome-wide libraries for
CRISPR screening.* Nature Methods 11:783–784.
[doi:10.1038/nmeth.3047](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.3047)

> lentiCRISPR v2 and the GeCKO v2 libraries. Short, and the supplement has the pooled cloning
> procedure with the array primers.

## Reading a screen out

**Joung J, et al. (2017).** *Genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 knockout and transcriptional activation
screening.* Nature Protocols 12:828–863.
[doi:10.1038/nprot.2017.016](https://doi.org/10.1038/nprot.2017.016) — **start here**

> A full protocol, including the one-PCR readout. Study the primer tables: which parts bind the
> vector, which are the sequencer handles, and why there are ten forward primers.

**Hart T, et al. (2015).** *High-resolution CRISPR screens reveal fitness genes and
genotype-specific cancer liabilities.* Cell 163:1515–1526.
[doi:10.1016/j.cell.2015.11.015](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2015.11.015)

> The screens that the Moffat-laboratory library and two-step readout were built for. Compare its
> readout with Joung's.

**Hiatt JB, et al. (2013).** *Single molecule molecular inversion probes for targeted,
high-accuracy detection of low-frequency variation.* Genome Research 23:843–854.
[doi:10.1101/gr.147686.112](https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.147686.112)

> The random tag that makes counting absolute. The idea transfers to any capture-then-count design.

## Screens with other readouts

**Datlinger P, et al. (2017).** *Pooled CRISPR screening with single-cell transcriptome readout.*
Nature Methods 14:297–301.
[doi:10.1038/nmeth.4177](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4177)

> CROP-seq: the LTR duplication used as a design tool. Trace exactly where the guide ends up.

**Tsai SQ, et al. (2015).** *GUIDE-seq enables genome-wide profiling of off-target cleavage by
CRISPR-Cas nucleases.* Nature Biotechnology 33:187–197.
[doi:10.1038/nbt.3117](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3117)

> A one-end-known mapping problem solved with a tag and an adapter. Follow the library
> construction figure in the supplement.

**Melnikov A, et al. (2012).** *Systematic dissection and optimization of inducible enhancers in
human cells using a massively parallel reporter assay.* Nature Biotechnology 30:271–277.
[doi:10.1038/nbt.2137](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.2137)

> MPRA: how a tag links each synthesised sequence to its read-out.

**Smith GP (1985).** *Filamentous fusion phage: novel expression vectors that display cloned antigens on the virion surface.* Science 228:1315–1317.
[doi:10.1126/science.4001944](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.4001944)

> The original display paper, and still the clearest statement of the idea the whole field
> rests on: put the protein on the outside of a particle that carries its own gene inside.
> Read it beside McCafferty, which turns the trick into antibody discovery.

**McCafferty J, Griffiths AD, Winter G, Chiswell DJ (1990).** *Phage antibodies: filamentous phage displaying antibody variable domains.* Nature 348:552–554.
[doi:10.1038/348552a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/348552a0)

> Why display matters for human biology: this is the route by which therapeutic antibodies
> are found. Note what the selection can and cannot ask for.

**Olson CA, et al. (2012).** *Single-round, multiplexed antibody mimetic design through mRNA display.* Angewandte Chemie International Edition 51:12449–12453.
[doi:10.1002/anie.201207005](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.201207005)

> The argument for sequencing a pool instead of panning it repeatedly. Look at what is gained
> by counting every variant rather than isolating the winners.

**Hill AJ, McFaline-Figueroa JL, Starita LM, Gasperini MJ, et al. (2018).** *On the design of CRISPR-based single-cell molecular screens.* Nature Methods 15:271–274.
[doi:10.1038/nmeth.4604](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4604) — **start here** before designing one

> Why the original barcode-proxy designs misassign guides: lentiviral recombination and
> template switching move a barcode onto the wrong guide, and the rate is high enough to
> matter. Read it for the measurement, then for what it implies — capture the guide itself.

  [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0003647](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0003647) — the two cloning methods
- Kosuri S, Church GM (2014), Nature Methods 11:499–507,
  [doi:10.1038/nmeth.2918](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.2918) — oligo synthesis on arrays
- Ochman H, et al. (1988), Genetics 120:621–623,
